content.overview: Section 169 provides that a company may, by ordinary resolution, remove a director (not being a director appointed by the Tribunal under section 242) before the expiry of the period of office after giving special notice. The director is entitled to be heard on the resolution. A vacancy created by removal may be filled at the meeting at which the director is removed if special notice of the intended appointment was given. An independent director re-appointed for a second term under section 149(10) is removable only by special resolution.
content.glance: Ordinary resolution after special notice; director entitled to be heard; Tribunal-appointed directors excluded; vacancy may be filled at same meeting if special notice of appointment given; second-term independent director needs special resolution.
content.study: A company may, by ordinary resolution, remove a director, not being a director appointed by the Tribunal under section 242, before the expiry of the period of his office after giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Special notice is required of any resolution to remove a director or to appoint somebody in place of a director so removed. On receipt of notice of an intended resolution to remove a director, the company must send a copy to the director concerned, who is entitled to be heard on the resolution at the meeting. A vacancy created by the removal of a director under this section may, if he had been appointed by the company in general meeting or by the Board under section 161, be filled by the appointment of another director in his place at the meeting at which he is removed, provided special notice of the intended appointment has been given. A director so appointed holds office until the date up to which his predecessor would have held office if he had not been removed. An independent director re-appointed for a second term on the Board under section 149(10) shall be removed by the company only by passing a special resolution and after giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Current-law framing: confirm special notice; ordinary (or special for second-term ID) resolution; opportunity of being heard; exclude Tribunal-appointed directors; apply vacancy-fill rules.

sections.heading: Power and Form
sections.body: Company may remove a director before expiry of term by ordinary resolution after special notice, with a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sections.heading: Excluded Directors
sections.body: A director appointed by the Tribunal under section 242 cannot be removed under this section. Nominee cases are subject to the limits stated in the Act and any governing agreement or law.

sections.heading: Hearing and Special Notice
sections.body: Special notice of the removal (and of any replacement appointment) is required; the director is entitled to be heard at the meeting.

sections.heading: Filling the Vacancy
sections.body: Vacancy may be filled at the same meeting if special notice of the intended appointment was given; the appointee holds for the remainder of the predecessor’s term.

sections.heading: Second-Term Independent Director
sections.body: An independent director re-appointed for a second term under s. 149(10) is removable only by special resolution after opportunity of being heard.

examples.title: Ordinary removal
examples.body: Members give special notice and pass an ordinary resolution removing a non-Tribunal director after the director is heard. Section 169 is satisfied.

examples.title: Second-term independent director
examples.body: An independent director is serving a second term under s. 149(10). Removal requires a special resolution under s. 169, not merely an ordinary resolution.

hypotheticals.question: Is removal under s. 169, without more, oppression under the Act?
hypotheticals.analysis: Removal by a valid ordinary (or special) resolution under section 169 is a statutory power. Whether the surrounding facts amount to oppression is a separate inquiry under the oppression and mismanagement provisions; removal alone is not automatically oppression.

distinctions.title: Removal (s. 169) vs vacation (s. 167) vs resignation (s. 168)
distinctions.right: Vacation is automatic; resignation is voluntary notice by the director

misconceptions.trap: Any director can be removed by ordinary resolution without special notice.
misconceptions.correction: Special notice is required, and the director is entitled to be heard. Second-term independent directors need a special resolution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 169 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm special notice and opportunity of hearing. II. Check ordinary vs special resolution (second-term ID). III. Exclude Tribunal-appointed directors. IV. Apply vacancy-fill rules. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Special notice facts; hearing; resolution type; excluded status if any; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 169 allows a company to remove a director before the end of the term by ordinary resolution after special notice and opportunity of being heard, with special rules for Tribunal-appointed and second-term independent directors.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Members retain the power to remove directors mid-term subject to procedural safeguards and limited statutory exclusions.
